title: Lucia di Lammermoor
facts: Lucia premiered on 26 September 1835 at the Teatro di San Carlo in Naples.
The libretto is loosely based on Walter Scott’s 1819 novel The Bride of Lammermoor, written when Scotland’s history and folklore were all the rage.
With Rossini retired and Bellini recently dead, Donizetti was left as “the sole reigning genius of Italian opera”.
Lucia was never absent from the Met’s repertory for more than one season at a time from 1903 until 1972.
After World War II, Maria Callas and Joan Sutherland gave the opera new life.

The mad scene has long been a coloratura showpiece. It gave Joan Sutherland her breakthrough.

Glass harmonica players revived Donizetti’s original scoring at La Scala in 2006, and it has since been heard in Lucia productions at the Met.
The Act II sextet features prominently in Martin Scorsese’s film The Departed.
For Paris, Donizetti revised the score into a French version, Lucie de Lammermoor, first given in 1839.
